sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Kumar Srivastava,Rupesh Kumar Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State/opposite party no.1 and perused the record with the assistance of learned counsel for the parties.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant to quash the impugned orders dated 27.02.2017 passed by Judicial Magistrate, Ist, Aonla, Bareilly, whereby application under Section 245 (2) Cr.P.C. dated 16.02.2017 of the applicant in Case No. 154 of 2012 under Sections 26, 27, 51, 52, 59 & 63 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, Police Station Aonla, District - Bareilly has been rejected and order dated 10.01.2020 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 15, Bareilly in Criminal Revision No. 155 of 2017 (CNR No. UPBR 01-003523-2017), whereby revision preferred by the applicat (Atul Bansal) has also been rejected.

sentences.text: Brief facts of this case as emerged from the record are that on 20.10.2011 on the direction of District Magistrate, an inspection of the shop/premises of firm Bansal brothers was carried out by Sunil Kumar, authorized officer in presence of R.N. Pandey, S.D.M., Aonla and samples of Besan and Ghee were taken by them.
Thereafter, samples were sent for analysis.

Food analyst submitted report no. 6595 dated 15.12.2011 regarding seized Besan with the opinion that 'according to regulation number 2.2.2-8, 2.2.2-9 and 2.2.2-10 of Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation 2011, manufacturer has not declared batch No., Mfg date and best before respectively on the empty packet and sample having fungus and non permitted synthetic colour Metanil Yellow which are harmful for human consumption.
Hence the sample is misbranded and unsafe'.

Another report no.
6589 dated 15.12.2011 was also submitted by Food Analyst regarding seized Ghee with the opinion that 'Butyrorefractometer Reading at 40.C exceeds to prescribed maximum limit of 43.0 for ghee and Richert value is much less than minimum limit of 26.0.
Hence, sample is substandard'.
Thereafter, required sanctioned for prosecution against the accused persons was also granted on 16.02.2012 by the Commissioner, Food Safety and Drug Administration U.P. Lucknow.

Food Safety Officer, Bareilly after completing all the required formalities filed complaint dated 23.02.2012 against applicant Atul Bansal and co-accused Anuj Bansal for violation of Section 26 (2) (i) (ii) (iii),
27 (2) ( c) of Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006 and Regulation no. 2.2.2-8, 2.2.2-9 and 2.2.2-10 of Food Safety and Standard (Packaging & Labeling) Regulation 2011, which are punishable under Section 51, 52, 59(i) and 63 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On 07.09.2013 charges have been framed against the applicant and co-accused Anuj Bansal.

After about three and half years,
applicant alongwith co-accused Anuj Bansal jointly moved an application under Section 245(2)
Cr.P.C., which was rejected by aforesaid impugned order dated 27.02.2017 and upheld by the revisional court vide order dated 10.01.2020.
Learned counsel for the applicant assailing the aforesaid impugned orders submits that both the aforesaid impugned orders have been passed without applying judicial mind.
The application under Section 245 (2) Cr.P.C. of the applicant has been illegally rejected in a cryptic manner.
Both the courts below have not gone through the materials available on record.

Lastly, it is submitted that no prima facie offence under Sections under Sections 26, 27, 51, 52, 59 & 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is made out against the applicant, therefore, impugned orders are liable to be quashed.
On the other hand learned AGA submits that in the present case trial has proceeded further.
Opposite party no.2/complainant has been examined as PW-1 and Rajeev Agarwal has been examined as PW-2 under Section 246 Cr.P.C.
This fact has been mentioned by the applicant in paragraph no. 18 of the application.
It is also submitted that it is well settled that disputed question of facts cannot be taken into consideration at the stage of deciding the application under Section 245 Cr.P.C.

Lastly, it is submitted that there is no illegality in the aforesaid impugned orders as the same have been passed in the light of well settled principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, therefore, application is liable to be dismissed.

After having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, I find that impugned orders dated 27.02.2017 and 10.01.2020 have been passed after considering the facts and materials on record of the case in accordance with law.

The impugned orders clearly reflect that Atul Bansal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185726398/
2 full application of mind has been applied by the courts concerned before passing the aforesaid impugned orders.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant also admitted that complainant/opposite party no.2 and Rajeev Agarwal have been examined as PW-1 and PW-2 under Section 246 Cr.P.C.
Revisional court has recorded specific finding that since in this case charge against the applicant has already been framed on 07.09.2013, therefore, application under Section 245(2) Cr.P.C. dated 16.02.2017 of the applicant, which was moved much after framing of charge was not maintainable.
Revisional court relying on the judgment of Apex Court in case of Rati Lal Vs. State of Maharashtra AIR 1979 SC 94 has further observed that once charge has been framed against accused, he cannot be discharged.
Revisional court considering the judgment of Apex Court in case of Sanghi brothers (Indore) Pvt.
Ltd. Vs. Sanjay Choudhary and others 2008 (10) SCC 681 has also observed that there is no error in the order dated 27.02.2017 passed by Judicial Magistrate, Ist, Aonla, Bareilly and it cannot be said that the concerned court below did not apply his judicial mind.

Sanghi brothers (Indore) Pvt.
Ltd. Vs. Sanjay Choudhary and others 2008 (10) SCC 681
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here, it it relevant to mention that the Apex Court in case of Palwinder Singh Vs. Balvinder Singh 2009 (3) SCC 850 has held that the jurisdiction of Sessions Judge at the time of discharge is very limited.

entities.text: Palwinder Singh Vs. Balvinder Singh 2009 (3) SCC 850
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said judgment it has been held that charges can also be framed on the basis of strong suspicion.
Marshaling and appreciation of evidence is not in the domain of the court at that point of time.

Apart from the aforesaid fact, it is also relevant to mention that in the present case application under Section 245(2) Cr.P.C. was moved on 16.02.2017 after framing of charge as well as after recording the statement of PW-1/complainant and PW-2 Rajeev Agarwal under Section 246 Cr.P.C.,
therefore, in the opinion of this Court no illegality has been committed by the concerned courts below in rejecting the application dated 16.02.2017 under Section 245(2) Cr.P.C. of the applicant.
In view of above, I do not find any illegality or irregularity in the aforesaid impugned orders,
therefore, same is not liable to be interfered.
Accordingly, application sans merit and stands dismissed.
